answer: Each newcomer locks a small refundable deposit for thirty days, so opening a garden of fake accounts ties up real money for a month instead of costing nothing. The network then maps who talks to whom: genuine users have messy, wide-ranging links, while a velvet of puppets mostly interacts within its own closed circle. When a cluster looks that tight, its deposits are frozen and reviewed, and a confirmed farm forfeits them all — the pigment the attacker hoped to gain is erased by the deposits they lose.
